q: What are the three ideas this lesson says you need to get good output from AI?
options: Give it your real material, say who the output is for, and specify the format you want
Pay for a subscription, install an app, and learn to code
Ask short questions, use English only, and type fast
Give it a role, wait 24 hours, then ask again
explanation: The lesson's three core moves: paste your real material, name the audience, and state the exact format. Everything else in the course builds on these.

q: Which of these do you need to complete this course?
options: A laptop with Microsoft Office installed
The free tier of ChatGPT or Gemini on a phone or laptop you already own
explanation: The course uses free tools only: ChatGPT free tier or Gemini free tier, on the device you already have. No code, no installations, no payment.

q: Why does the demo prompt include 'Do not invent anything that is not in the notes'?
options: To stop the AI from adding made-up details to your official record
Because AI works faster with shorter prompts
It is just polite phrasing with no effect
explanation: AI fills gaps with plausible-sounding invention. For a report that carries your name, you must tell it to stick to the material you gave it — and still check the output yourself.

q: Which of these is safest to paste into a free AI tool?
options: A payroll sheet with staff names and salaries
Patient or customer records with full names
Rough notes you wrote yourself, with confidential details removed
explanation: Notes you wrote yourself, with confidential details stripped out, are safe. Salaries, personal data of others and unpublished documents should never go into a free AI tool.
